21:1.sourceText: Μετὰ ταῦτα ἐφανέρωσεν ἑαυτὸν πάλιν Ἰησοῦς τοῖς μαθηταῖς ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης τῆς Τιβεριάδος· ἐφανέρωσεν δὲ οὕτως.
21:1.targetText: Later, by the Sea of Tiberias, Jesus again revealed Himself to the disciples. He made Himself known in this way:

groups.note: Μετὰ ταῦτα ("after these things") is rendered Later.
ἑαυτόν is understood again with the second ἐφανέρωσεν, where BSB repeats Himself.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB starts a new sentence instead of rendering δέ.

21:2.sourceText: ἦσαν ὁμοῦ Σίμων Πέτρος καὶ Θωμᾶς ὁ λεγόμενος Δίδυμος καὶ Ναθαναὴλ ὁ ἀπὸ Κανᾶ τῆς Γαλιλαίας καὶ οἱ τοῦ Ζεβεδαίου καὶ ἄλλοι ἐκ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ δύο.
21:2.targetText: Simon Peter, Thomas called Didymus, Nathanael from Cana in Galilee, the sons of Zebedee, and two other disciples were together.

groups.note: Article and participle ὁ λεγόμενος form one unit.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB lists the names with commas instead of rendering καί.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The partitive ἐκ ("of") is not rendered; BSB writes two other disciples.
BSB leaves αὐτοῦ ("His") unexpressed.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the family noun; the Greek has only the article with the genitive (οἱ τοῦ Ζεβεδαίου, "those of Zebedee").

21:3.sourceText: λέγει αὐτοῖς Σίμων Πέτρος Ὑπάγω ἁλιεύειν. λέγουσιν αὐτῷ Ἐρχόμεθα καὶ ἡμεῖς σὺν σοί. ἐξῆλθον καὶ ἐνέβησαν εἰς τὸ πλοῖον, καὶ ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ νυκτὶ ἐπίασαν οὐδέν.
21:3.targetText: Simon Peter told them, “I am going fishing.”  “We will go with you,” they said. So they went out and got into the boat, but caught nothing that night.

groups.note: The present Ἐρχόμεθα ("we are coming") is rendered will go.

unmappedSource.reason: The indirect object αὐτῷ ("to him") is not rendered.
BSB leaves καί ("also") unexpressed.
BSB states the time as that night, without a preposition for ἐν.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds a connective; the Greek has none here.

21:4.sourceText: πρωΐας δὲ ἤδη γινομένης ἔστη Ἰησοῦς εἰς τὸν αἰγιαλόν· οὐ μέντοι ᾔδεισαν οἱ μαθηταὶ ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ἐστιν.
21:4.targetText: Early in the morning, Jesus stood on the shore, but the disciples did not recognize that it was Jesus.

groups.note: The genitive absolute πρωΐας γινομένης ("as morning was coming") is rendered Early in the morning; BSB's Greek differs slightly here, with the same sense.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
BSB leaves ἤδη ("already") unexpressed.

21:5.sourceText: λέγει οὖν αὐτοῖς Ἰησοῦς Παιδία, μή τι προσφάγιον ἔχετε; ἀπεκρίθησαν αὐτῷ Οὔ.
21:5.targetText: So He called out to them, “Children, do you have any fish?”  “No,” they answered.

groups.note: BSB has named Jesus just before, so Ἰησοῦς is rendered He.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB renders the question particle μή (expecting "no") as a plain question.
The indirect object αὐτῷ ("to Him") is not rendered.

21:6.sourceText: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Βάλετε εἰς τὰ δεξιὰ μέρη τοῦ πλοίου τὸ δίκτυον, καὶ εὑρήσετε. ἔβαλον οὖν, καὶ οὐκέτι αὐτὸ ἑλκύσαι ἴσχυον ἀπὸ τοῦ πλήθους τῶν ἰχθύων.
21:6.targetText: He told them, “Cast the net on the right side of the boat, and you will find some.” So they cast it there, and they were unable to haul it in because of the great number of fish.

groups.note: In ὁ δέ the article serves as the pronoun he.
οὐκέτι ἴσχυον ("they were no longer able") is rendered they were unable.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for find; the Greek has none.
English supplies the object and place for cast; the Greek has none.

21:7.sourceText: λέγει οὖν ὁ μαθητὴς ἐκεῖνος ὃν ἠγάπα ὁ Ἰησοῦς τῷ Πέτρῳ Ὁ Κύριός ἐστιν. Σίμων οὖν Πέτρος, ἀκούσας ὅτι ὁ Κύριός ἐστιν, τὸν ἐπενδύτην διεζώσατο, ἦν γὰρ γυμνός, καὶ ἔβαλεν ἑαυτὸν εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν·
21:7.targetText: Then the disciple whom Jesus loved said to Peter, “It is the Lord!” As soon as Simon Peter heard that it was the Lord, he put on his outer garment (for he had removed it) and jumped into the sea.

groups.note: The participle ἀκούσας ("having heard") is rendered As soon as … heard.
ἦν … γυμνός ("he was stripped") is rendered he had removed it.
ἔβαλεν ἑαυτόν ("threw himself") is rendered jumped.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the demonstrative ἐκεῖνος ("that") unexpressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The connective οὖν is not separately expressed; As soon as belongs to the participle.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object, the outer garment; the Greek has none.

21:8.sourceText: οἱ δὲ ἄλλοι μαθηταὶ τῷ πλοιαρίῳ ἦλθον, οὐ γὰρ ἦσαν μακρὰν ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς ἀλλὰ ὡς ἀπὸ πηχῶν διακοσίων, σύροντες τὸ δίκτυον τῶν ἰχθύων.
21:8.targetText: The other disciples came ashore in the boat. They dragged in the net full of fish, for they were not far from land, only about a hundred yards.

groups.note: The dative τῷ πλοιαρίῳ ("by the boat") is rendered in the boat.
After the negative, ἀλλά ("but") is rendered only.
πηχῶν διακοσίων ("two hundred cubits") is converted to a hundred yards.
The participle σύροντες ("dragging") is rendered as a new sentence.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
ἀπό marks the distance ("off by"), which English gives without a preposition.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds where they came; ἦλθον ("came") has no such word.
English describes the net of fish as full; the Greek has only the genitive.

21:9.sourceText: ὡς οὖν ἀπέβησαν εἰς τὴν γῆν, βλέπουσιν ἀνθρακιὰν κειμένην καὶ ὀψάριον ἐπικείμενον καὶ ἄρτον.
21:9.targetText: When they landed, they saw a charcoal fire there with fish on it, and some bread.

groups.note: ἀπέβησαν εἰς τὴν γῆν ("got out onto the land") is rendered landed.
κειμένην ("lying") is rendered there.
καί joining the fish to the fire is rendered with.
ἐπικείμενον ("lying on") is rendered on it.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective οὖν is not separately expressed; When renders ὡς.

21:10.sourceText: λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ἐνέγκατε ἀπὸ τῶν ὀψαρίων ὧν ἐπιάσατε νῦν.
21:10.targetText: Jesus told them, “Bring some of the fish you have just caught.”

groups.note: νῦν ("now") is rendered just.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves the relative pronoun ὧν ("which") unexpressed.

21:11.sourceText: ἀνέβη Σίμων Πέτρος καὶ εἵλκυσεν τὸ δίκτυον εἰς τὴν γῆν μεστὸν ἰχθύων μεγάλων ἑκατὸν πεντήκοντα τριῶν· καὶ τοσούτων ὄντων οὐκ ἐσχίσθη τὸ δίκτυον.
21:11.targetText: So Simon Peter went aboard and dragged the net ashore. It was full of large fish, 153, but even with so many, the net was not torn.

groups.note: εἰς τὴν γῆν ("to the land") is rendered ashore.
ἑκατὸν πεντήκοντα τριῶν ("a hundred fifty-three") is written as one numeral.
The concessive genitive absolute τοσούτων ὄντων ("though there were so many") is rendered even with so many.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB follows a reading with an extra word here.
English starts a new sentence with It was; μεστόν ("full") describes the net.

21:12.sourceText: λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Δεῦτε ἀριστήσατε. οὐδεὶς ἐτόλμα τῶν μαθητῶν ἐξετάσαι αὐτόν Σὺ τίς εἶ; εἰδότες ὅτι ὁ Κύριός ἐστιν.
21:12.targetText: “Come, have breakfast,” Jesus said to them. None of the disciples dared to ask Him, “Who are You?” They knew it was the Lord.

21:13.sourceText: ἔρχεται Ἰησοῦς καὶ λαμβάνει τὸν ἄρτον καὶ δίδωσιν αὐτοῖς, καὶ τὸ ὀψάριον ὁμοίως.
21:13.targetText: Jesus came and took the bread and gave it to them, and He did the same with the fish.

groups.note: ὁμοίως ("likewise") is rendered the same.

English supplies a subject and verb; the Greek καὶ τὸ ὀψάριον ὁμοίως has none.
English links the fish to the repeated action; the Greek has no preposition.

21:14.sourceText: τοῦτο ἤδη τρίτον ἐφανερώθη Ἰησοῦς τοῖς μαθηταῖς ἐγερθεὶς ἐκ νεκρῶν.
21:14.targetText: This was now the third time that Jesus appeared to the disciples after He was raised from the dead.

groups.note: The participle ἐγερθείς ("having been raised") is rendered after He was raised.

21:15.targetText: When they had finished eating, Jesus asked Simon Peter, “Simon son of John, do you love Me more than these?”  “Yes, Lord,” he answered, “You know I love You.”  Jesus replied, “Feed My lambs.”

21:18.sourceText: ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω σοι, ὅτε ἦς νεώτερος, ἐζώννυες σεαυτὸν καὶ περιεπάτεις ὅπου ἤθελες· ὅταν δὲ γηράσῃς, ἐκτενεῖς τὰς χεῖράς σου, καὶ ἄλλος ζώσει σε καὶ οἴσει ὅπου οὐ θέλεις.
21:18.targetText: Truly, truly, I tell you, when you were young, you dressed yourself and walked where you wanted; but when you are old, you will stretch out your hands, and someone else will dress you and lead you where you do not want to go.”

21:19.targetText: Jesus said this to indicate the kind of death by which Peter would glorify God.  And after He had said this, He told him, “Follow Me.”
